newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks drift weakly close ahead of issues.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks drift weakly close ahead of issues.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares drifted to a weak close on Monday with dealers saying some older stocks seemed to have gone to sleep ahead of new issues due in March.

The key industrial index shed 48.84 points to end at 10,650.95, dragged lower largely by newly-listed TZI TZI.ZI 's 110-cent drop to 750, bankers Barclays and clothing retailer Edgars' 's 100-cent losses each to 3,600 and 5,000 respectively.

"The market is drifting off a little bit. Some of the older shares have gone to sleep on the new issues. I think the market is taking a breather and this gives rise to opportunities for bargain hunting," a dealer said.
"Underlying sentiment is a bit cautious at the moment but it's still bullish on the year," he added.

Also among the day's losers, farming implement-maker Zimplow cut 100 cents to 800 while Alloys at 600, food group Natfoods at 550, furniture and clothing retailer Tedco at 1,100 and publishers Zimpapers at 3,100 all shed 50 cents.

Against the trend, cigarette manufacturer Rothmans surged 250 cents to 5,000, steel-window maker Radar leapt 100 cents to 600, supermarkets and hotel group Meikles rose 50 cents to 2,850 and tyre manufacturer Dunlop added 20 cents to 230.
Minings continued to gain support on the back of a steadily rising gold price and historically cheap fundamentals on the mining board.
Falgold put on five cents to 70 as did Alloys Mines to 115. The mining index ended 4.95 points to 906.01.
